steps.sameNumber: The number doesn’t tell the whole story. {c} to {e} and {d} to {f} are both thirds, but the first is wider. Count the half steps: four make a major third, three a minor third.
steps.perfect: Fourths, fifths and octaves have one usual size, so they’re called perfect: five half steps for a perfect fourth, seven for a perfect fifth and twelve for an octave. From {c}, that’s {f}, {g} and {c} again.
steps.nameThem: Count the half steps between the two notes, and name the interval.
steps.build: Now build them: count up the half steps from the note given.
steps.others: Seconds, sixths and sevenths come in major and minor too. A minor second is one half step and a major second two; a minor sixth is eight and a major sixth nine; a minor seventh is ten and a major seventh eleven.
steps.allOfThem: All of them together. Take your time: only your first answer counts.
